study.question: Can 16 direct action-by-age counts replace the 16-dimensional learned history summary while retaining the 32 supported target count/freshness values? Does additional action/time association help beyond the same global action and age marginals? Observed limitation: removing the semantic summary gives scalar_time AUC 0.617348249 versus attention_time 0.618663774, whereas global_mean reaches 0.618483291, only 0.000180484 below attention_control. Thus a cheap summary retains most of the observed AUC, but it is unknown whether entity identity or temporal distribution supplies its value.
study.hypothesis: A coarse action-by-age distribution may recover part of the scalar-only AUC loss by making temporal shape directly accessible, without per-event learned embeddings or scoring. The additional joint distribution may outperform a product-of-marginals reconstruction if age distribution by action contains useful detail beyond inherited one-day mean decay. This is a falsifiable local representation hypothesis, not a verified new general method. Trajectory review: references static/pooled/DIN yielded AUC 0.605003614/0.610226114/0.613361986. The round-0 fixed-width factorial yielded repeat/count/freshness/both AUC 0.612922535/0.618067894/0.615610452/0.618663774: counts dominate, freshness adds a smaller benefit with counts. Round 1 target_presence/target_time achieved 0.618313568/0.618663774, versus activity_presence/activity_time 0.613738085/0.613809977: target groups matter more than that time substitution. Round 2 scalar_time/scalar_presence 0.617348249/0.615663682 versus attention_time/attention_presence 0.618663774/0.618313568 shows temporal values matter more without the summary. Round 3 matched_mean/global_mean/matched_attention/attention_control 0.618208698/0.618483291/0.618273437/0.618663774 does not support hard match selection; this branch is not continued. All are successful executions; the unsuccessful directions are scientific negatives, not runtime failures. No previous_runtime_error is present. Global_mean versus scalar_time AUC differs by 0.001135042, but Logloss is worse for global_mean (0.196113473 versus 0.196023190), so recovery of primary AUC must not conceal the calibration tradeoff.

nearest_work.difference: DIN describes learned event pooling, target-conditioned activation and explicitly preserves intensity by omitting softmax (lines 272-277). We inherit static embedding/MLP and local references, but compare a fixed, label-free four-action/four-age count table to its product marginals and redundant counts. The local attention reference uses normalized softmax and field substitutions; it is not an exact DIN reproduction. Count preservation, histograms, and feature engineering are not claimed novel. Authorized paper searches for pooling, temporal and time returned no additional sources; broader nearest-work coverage and priority remain unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Predeclare disjoint age bins [0,3600), [3600,86400), [86400,604800), [604800,infinity) seconds without fitting boundaries to validation. Compute J[a,t] from all supplied masked-in events, flatten action-major, transform log1p(J)/log(129), and use it as the same 16-wide summary slot. Independent control uses I[a,t]=sum_t(J[a,t])*sum_a(J[a,t])/max(sum(J),1), then the same transform. This preserves both count marginals before transformation and deletes only their joint association in this slot. Repeat control places the existing full C block in the slot; it adds no information and tests duplicated-feature optimization effects. Mean control uses the inherited global masked mean. All variants compute J and I, retaining identical registered module shapes; histogram and repeat variants skip event embeddings and scorer. There is no additional information source, wider head, changed sample coverage, loss, optimizer, or data pass. Local checks: all four standalone modules compile, use permitted numeric imports, have identical Model ASTs, and preserve learned-construction and evidence ASTs against the ancestor. A standard-library pure-Python mathematical reference passed 103 empty/boundary/random cases for masking, permutation, conservation, finite transforms and marginal preservation, plus an association contrast. These checks do not execute Torch or establish logits, model performance, GPU cost, or full-population mechanism evidence; host execution is required.
predictions: Primary: joint_histogram AUC exceeds repeat_counts under the frozen full protocol; compare Logloss separately. Failing to improve on a duplicate-information control weakens the temporal-shape hypothesis.

Association subhypothesis: joint_histogram AUC exceeds independent_histogram; a tie supports at most marginals/representation utility. Since inherited T retains action-conditioned time, the contrast concerns additional distribution detail only.

Practical compression target: joint_histogram AUC is within 0.0003 absolute of same-round mean_control and the inherited attention incumbent, with lower measured training cost/peak memory. This tolerance is an engineering screen, not a statistical equivalence claim. Any gain/loss and Logloss tradeoff must be reported.

Implementation: histogram count conservation error=0; action reference error=0; independence marginal errors <=0.0001 (float32 tolerance); empty histogram=0; all host logits/diagnostic scalars finite. Bins should not be all empty on nonempty rows.

Exploratory slices: report the frozen host history-length, hour, behavior-presence, category-match, and training-frequency slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Existing long-history slice is 3026583 rows, 151372 positives, 2875211 negatives; do not treat its dominance or slice differences as independent evidence. Do not invent unavailable missing-field slice feedback.
falsifiers: joint_histogram fails to beat repeat_counts: no support for useful extra temporal-distribution evidence in this implementation. Independent and joint both losing to mean_control would favor residual identity information or learned coordinates; it would not refute all compact alternatives.

joint_histogram does not beat independent_histogram: no support for incremental action/time joint structure beyond the retained features and marginals. If independent wins, prefer that simpler explanation and retain the negative result.
repeat_counts improves similarly to joint_histogram: duplicated input pathways or optimization explain apparent gains; do not attribute them to new temporal information.

mean_control materially fails to reproduce g0-r0003-global_mean or invariant checks fail: diagnose implementation/runtime differences before interpreting mechanism comparisons. Failed runs remain charged; do not automatically duplicate unknown-state executions.

AUC differences reverse across paired seeds, user-cluster intervals include important losses, or measured cost is not lower: do not claim robust quality retention, efficiency, or repeated mechanism support. No interval will be fabricated if the host does not supply bootstrap access.
alternative_explanations: Single-seed validation comparisons are preliminary. Repeated deterministic reference receipts are reproducibility evidence, not independent seeds or independent mechanism contrasts.
The inherited T block retains per-action and per-target-group mean exponential age. Association is removed only from the additional histogram slot, not from the whole model.
Joint counts are integral and sparse; independence counts can be fractional and dense. Log1p changes coordinates, so a difference supports this representation, not a causal behavioral mechanism.
History truncation, nonzero supplied-bucket matching, possible hashing collisions, and undocumented static snapshot as-of dates remain inherited limitations.
Mean vectors preserve historical category/brand identities absent from histograms. Histogram versus mean is a replacement and quality/cost comparison, not an isolated test of time versus identity.

Histogram wins could result from scale, sparsity, inductive bias, or checkpoint selection rather than a uniquely correct behavioral mechanism. Joint versus independent keeps count scale/marginals/head fixed but cannot eliminate coordinate/optimization effects.
Coarse bins may be insufficient or poorly located; a negative implementation does not refute richer temporal summaries. No bin tuning is performed against this round after observing outcomes.

Registered parameter counts are equal, but dormant modules and shared embedding gradient paths differ. This study tests forward-computation replacement; it does not establish a smaller stored model or an equal-compute optimum. Batch inference latency includes host feature gathering and can be noisy.
